speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after a tympanoplasty; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if they happen when you touch the ear canal?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Suppurative Otitis Media (CSOM) with a persistent cholesteatoma or recurrent granulation tissue in the right ear.

The combination of shooting pain when eating (referred pain via the auriculotemporal nerve or tensor tympani), discomfort with earrings (suggesting a bony protrusion or granulation tissue), and your history of chronic ear infections despite a recent successful tympanoplasty strongly points to a recurrence or a specific complication like a cholesteatoma. I need to see the ear canal immediately to confirm this. REQUEST IMAGES: Right Ear Otoscopy.
